_description: Output schema for the general SAST triager. The agent reads this file alongside SKILL.md and emits triage-output.json conforming to this shape. Placeholder strings in angle brackets describe expected content; for fields with a fixed enumeration, the placeholder shows the allowed values separated by ' | '.
category: When triage_decision is TRUE POSITIVE: exactly 'N/A'. When triage_decision is UNCLEAR: exactly 'N/A'. When triage_decision is FALSE POSITIVE: one of: FP - NOISE:NotSecret | FP - NOISE:NotSensitiveDataLeak | FP - NOISE:Mismatch | FP - TRIVIAL:TestCode | FP - TRIVIAL:NotInProd | FP - TRIVIAL:NoRiskToCase | FP - TRIVIAL:NoRiskToModule | FP - THEORETICAL:NoExternalInput | FP - THEORETICAL:TrustedExternalNonhumanInput | FP - THEORETICAL:DevOpsCode | FP - THEORETICAL:TaintFlowNotFeasible | FP - THEORETICAL:BenignUse | FP - MITIGATED:InputValidation | FP - MITIGATED:SecureCode | FP - MITIGATED:SecureConfig | FP - MITIGATED:ApprovedCompensatingControl | FP - OTHERS.
additional_category: Same allowed values as category, or 'N/A'. Use to record a secondary FP reason when multiple apply.
vulnerability_class: <e.g. SSRF, XSS, XXE, Path Traversal, SQL Injection, Weak Cryptography, Insecure Deserialization, etc.>
summary: <one plain-language sentence stating the finding and verdict>
code_snippet: <3-5 lines of source as it appears in the file, verbatim, with a leading // Line N-M comment>
code_summary: <one sentence describing what the code does>
search_description: <brief note on identifiers, routes, callers traced>
external_input: TRUE | FALSE | UNCLEAR | <empty string if config issue or N/A>
sink_usage: Dangerous | Secure API | Secure Config | Benign Use | UNCLEAR | <empty>
key_facts: <3-8 declarative sentences, each citing concrete evidence>
additional_observations: <empty array unless an insight does not fit any other field>
